nodes.title: Hold the like state in a signal
nodes.why: liked drives three bindings at once, the active class, aria-pressed and the Like or Liked label, so one signal keeps all three in step under OnPush.
nodes.alternative: A plain liked field, which still updates here because only the button's click changes it.
nodes.tradeoff: Each binding pays a function call; a plain field would stop updating under OnPush once something outside the click handler, such as a server reply, set it.

nodes.title: Store the count next to the like
nodes.why: count is its own state starting at 120, moved by one on every toggle, and the number beside the button reads count().
nodes.alternative: Derive it with computed(() => 120 + (this.liked() ? 1 : 0)), so the count can never disagree with liked.
nodes.tradeoff: Two signals mirror the starter and the spec's clamp but must always change together; a computed removes that risk but hard-codes the starting number.

nodes.title: Branch on the current like state
nodes.why: Reading liked() once decides both writes, the new like state and the direction of the count, so the label, the style and the number cannot disagree after a click.
nodes.alternative: Flip liked first and read it back to decide the count, or render separate Like and Unlike buttons.
nodes.tradeoff: One handler with an early return is easy to follow; flipping first and re-reading also works but makes the order of the two writes matter.

nodes.title: Change both signals in the same handler
nodes.why: Both writes finish before Angular renders again, so the active style, the label and 121 appear together after the click.
nodes.alternative: Set only liked and let an effect that watches it adjust count.
nodes.tradeoff: An effect would keep count in sync without the handler's help but runs later and hides the cause; two explicit writes keep the whole rule in toggleLike().

nodes.title: Never let the count drop below zero
nodes.why: Taking a like back subtracts one through Math.max, the guard the spec asks for; starting from 120 it never triggers, but it holds for a post whose count starts at 0 while already liked.
nodes.alternative: Subtract without a guard and trust the toggle to keep the count consistent.
nodes.tradeoff: The guard is unreachable from this UI and costs one call; it keeps the rule true if the starting count or the initial like state ever changes.
